title: Divisibility and parity in the natural numbers
introduction: Divisibility begins with a factor witness. The same idea explains why divisibility passes through sums and products, and why adding an even increment preserves parity.

glossary.definition: A natural number that exhibits the required product for a divisibility claim. For an expression of evenness as a sum of two equal terms, it is the repeated summand.
Divisible by two. The second section gives the equivalent description as a sum of two equal terms.
The claim at the current index, assumed only while proving the claim at its successor.

sections.title: Divisibility and its closure rules
sections.introduction: The first five results exhibit witnesses directly. The remaining results show how to combine witnesses or use the resulting closure rules.

sections.title: Even numbers
sections.introduction: Specializing divisibility to the divisor two gives both a witness description of even numbers and methods for proving that sums and products are even.
